scenes.text: Nobody broke in. Your Supabase app simply handed every user's profile to anyone who asked. Claude caught it.
Your frontend talks to Supabase directly, with the anon key. That key is public. That part is fine.
But the profiles table had Row Level Security switched off. So one line in the browser console returned everyone.
Claude turned it on, and wrote a policy: each user can only read the row whose id matches their own.
Same query. Same public key. Now it returns exactly one row. Yours.
If the browser can reach a table, that table needs a policy.
